Climate-Shock Energy Risk

Gulf hurricanes and US winter storms vs oil and gas prices, regime models and VaR · EIA data to 2026-09-22

Report (PDF)Models: regime-riskGitHub
OverviewEventsPrice responseRegimesVaR in stormsStress tests

When a hurricane crosses the Gulf of Mexico or a winter storm freezes the country, what happens to oil and gas prices, do standard risk models see it coming, and what would it cost a trading book? Events are chosen by physical rules (storm tracks, disaster damage), never by what prices did, and every result is compared with random days from the same season.

What the data say

The detail behind each answer is in the other tabs

QuestionEvidenceAnswer
Do winter storms move gas volatility?1.58x vs 0.81x, placebo p 0.005✔ Yes (FDR 10%)
Do hurricanes move oil volatility?0.99x vs 0.96x, placebo p 0.751✖ No
Does a real-time regime filter notice winter storms (gas)?shift +0.28, q 0.003✔ Yes
Does plain historical-simulation VaR fail in storms (gas)?3.4% vs 0.9%, Fisher p <0.001✔ Yes
Does the climate overlay cut storm breaches (book, filtered HS)?5 -> 2 breaches for 1.1% more average VaR✔ Yes, cheaply

Every event on the price history

Vertical lines: day 0 of each hurricane (pink) and winter storm (purple)

Hurricanes: NOAA best tracks, at hurricane strength inside the northern Gulf box (25.5-30.5°N, 98.0-86.0°W: offshore oil and gas and the Texas-to-Alabama refineries). Winter storms: NOAA NCEI billion-dollar winter storms and freezes, November to March. Day 0 is the first trading day on or after the event date.
